cards.b: Positive: points rise left to right. Negative: points fall. None: no pattern.
Strong: points close to a straight line. Weak: widely scattered.
Correlation does not prove one variable causes the other. A third factor may cause both (e.g. temperature, ice cream and drowning).
A point that clearly does not fit the pattern. It may be an error and can be ignored when drawing the line.

cards.f: Drawing a line of best fit
cards.b: Plot the mean point (x̄, ȳ), draw a straight line through it following the trend with points balanced either side.

cards.f: Equation of a line of best fit
cards.b: y = a + bx. b = gradient = change in y ÷ change in x (use points far apart). a = y-intercept.
In context: for each extra unit of x, y increases (or decreases) by about b.
The expected y when x = 0. Only meaningful if x = 0 makes sense.
Predicting within the range of the data. Reliable if the correlation is strong.
Predicting outside the range of the data. Unreliable because the pattern may not continue.
rs = 1 − 6Σd² ÷ (n(n² − 1)), where d = difference in ranks and n = number of pairs.
Rank both variables the same way (both from highest, or both from lowest). Rank each separately.
1: rankings agree exactly (perfect positive). −1: rankings exactly reversed (perfect negative).
Always between −1 and 1. If you get a value outside, recheck Σd².
Say strength and direction with context, e.g. 'strong positive: students good at maths tend to be good at science'.

short.q: Six students are ranked in two subjects. Ranks in Maths: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6. Ranks in Art: 2, 1, 4, 3, 6, 5. Calculate Spearman's rank correlation coefficient and interpret it. [4]
short.model: d = 1, −1, 1, −1, 1, −1 so Σd² = 6. rs = 1 − (6 × 6) ÷ (6 × 35) = 1 − 36/210 = 0.829. Strong positive correlation: students ranked high in Maths tend to be ranked high in Art.

short.q: A line of best fit passes through (4, 30) and (10, 48). Find its equation in the form y = a + bx. [3]
The number of fire engines at a fire and the damage caused show strong positive correlation. Does sending more fire engines cause more damage? Explain. [2]
short.model: No. Correlation does not prove causation. A third factor, the size of the fire, causes both more engines to be sent and more damage.
points: size of fire is a third factor

short.q: A line of best fit is y = 20 + 3x, drawn from data with x between 2 and 9. Use it to predict y when x = 20 and comment on the reliability. [2]
short.model: y = 20 + 3 × 20 = 80. This is extrapolation (20 is outside 2 to 9), so it is unreliable.

short.q: State two things you should do when drawing a line of best fit on a scatter diagram. [2]
short.model: Plot the mean point and draw a straight line (with a ruler) through it, following the trend with roughly equal numbers of points either side.
points: straight line following trend, points balanced either side
